I am beginning to suspect the order of static destructor execution here. It would not surprise me that the ordering across compilation units is deterministic for a particular toolchain, even if it is (I believe) technically undefined. And the ordering just happens to be such on macOS that the mutex gets destroyed before its last use. 

I'm unsure yet of exactly how to prove this let alone actually fix. But it does seem believable.

The crash is consistent, and points to something wrong with the mutex protecting `ScriptServer::global_classes`. So I just heap-allocated that variable and allowed it to leak. This changed the crash to a different static `HashMap` in `ClassDB`. I repeated the experiment there, and yes, and it did move to yet another static `HashMap`.

So, I feel pretty convinced that this experiment validates the hypothesis. The ordering of static destructors is the issue, for some reason only on macOS.

What I'm not sure of is if this is a configuration issue, an Apple toolchain implementation issue, or just bad luck. I also do not have a good grasp on what a reasonable solution could be. There are a bunch of statics spread out around the code base. I'd love some guidance on what might be a good avenue for a possible fix.

I was able to get the same crash. It looks like its an issue with calling exit() right after completion. That skips the Main::cleanup() call which results in not cleaning up resources properly and a crash depending on static destruction ordering.

@HolonProduction suggested that I try to apply https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117821 and also replace the call to exit with `OS::get_singleton()->set_exit_code(failed);`. This combination worked!

This solution also worked for me. I do get the same crash from calling exit(-1) to early out if I use the old --gdscript-generate-tests  flag instead of the new --test gdscript-generate-tests flag, but that is separate from this issue.

Yeah decided to not address that, changing the exit procedure there would be pretty useless given that the path is only kept for compat and to prompt people to use the new arg.
